gemini-2.5-flash.standardized_narrative: The syndicate reported a significant prior year reserve release of GBP 50.391 million in 2023, representing 19.68% of its opening gross claims outstanding. This favorable development primarily stemmed from strong underwriting results and positive investment activities across the 2022 and 2021 & prior years of account. A key contributing factor was the successful execution of a split-Reinsurance to Close (RITC) and Loss Portfolio Transfer (LPT) for 2018 and prior liabilities, and 2020 liabilities, which provided greater certainty and contributed to the profit. While 2023 saw elevated property catastrophe activity from events like Tropical Cyclone Gabrielle, Canadian wildfires, and Hurricane Otis-Mexico, incurred losses were broadly within budget. The syndicate also noted a clearer landscape for COVID-19 provisions, with an ultimate loss of GBP 3.7 million.

This arrangement has delivered a bespoke solution to help meet Syndicate 1492's strategic objectives and provides greater certainty as Syndicate 1492 continues to grow and diversify its business profitably.

Property catastrophe activity within the Syndicate's exposure footprint was more elevated than in previous years. However, incurred losses from cyclones and flooding in New Zealand, Canadian wildfires and Hurricane Otis were broadly within property catastrophe budgets.
The landscape for Covid-19 is now clearer than during or immediately after the pandemic.

GBP 50.39m (a release), driven primarily by favourable claims development and material reinsurance-related items (including reinsurance recoveries and the effect of a bespoke LPT/split-RITC arrangement), together with investment returns. The net effect was a reduction in gross claims outstanding at year end. Specific major loss events (e.g. Tropical Cyclone Gabrielle, Canada wildfires and Hurricane Otis) were identified but were broadly within catastrophe budgets and did not prevent an overall prior-year release.
